**No—do not approve the $1,000-a-day plan.** October 19 through December 31 is 74 days: that plan costs approximately $74,000, exceeding your $45,000 budget by $29,000. Your available average is about $608 a day.

I would use this phased budget, with increases conditional on profitability:

- **October 19–November 1:** $300/day; $4,200.
- **November 2–22:** up to $500/day; $10,500.
- **November 23–30:** up to $1,000/day; $8,000.
- **December:** up to $500/day; $15,500.

That allocates **$38,200**, leaving **$6,800** to extend profitable periods or fund gradual increases. These are spending ceilings, not commitments. Reduce December spending after your reliable holiday delivery cutoff unless demand remains profitable.

Before increasing, calculate contribution per first order: revenue after discounts, less product cost, fulfillment, shipping subsidies, payment fees, and expected returns. Keep acquisition cost below that contribution initially. Your reported 3.2 ROAS implies about $18.13 per attributed bottle at full price, assuming one bottle per order; it does not establish incremental new-customer acquisition cost. Separate new customers from returning buyers, inspect click-only results, and reconcile advertising with store revenue and contribution.

Do not justify losses using the 30% reorder rate until repeat-order margins and timing are verified; many new customers will reorder after December.

At unchanged reported efficiency, $45,000 implies approximately 2,483 bottles. Reserve inventory for organic purchases and existing customers’ reorders too. Forecast total weekly demand now. A manufacturer order placed today arrives around December 28, assuming ten weeks holds. If projected demand threatens stock, reduce acquisition spending early; replenishment offers little protection for Black Friday or Christmas.
